correctness.rationale: The primary source's balancing equations are applied to the triangular and square two-faces of the standard product, forcing one weight per simplex factor. The factor-\(i\) edge multiplicity is exactly \(Vd_i/2\), so the normalized type polytope is \(\sum d_i\lambda_i=D\) with the weighted Euclidean metric inherited from edge coordinates. The isometric variables \(y_i=\sqrt{Vd_i/2}\lambda_i\) turn the affine hull into a coordinate simplex with normal \((\sqrt{d_i})\). Projecting each coordinate normal into the affine tangent space gives the exact facet-distance formula, and equalizing those distances yields the displayed unique incenter and inradius. Disjoint edge-class supports give the exact pairwise vertex distances; with at least three vertices they are all equal exactly when the factor dimensions are equal.

source_inspections.trigger: Primary geometry-classified source defining the edge-weight type polytope and proving simplex type polytopes for products of simplices.

value.rationale: The type polytope is the primary source's normalized parameter space for weak Minkowski summands modulo translation and dilation, so its intrinsic Euclidean clearance from boundary faces is a natural robustness measure for deformations rather than an arbitrary statistic. The theorem determines that metric exactly for every standard product of simplices, identifies the unique most interior normalized deformation, and shows how factor dimensions bias the center through complementary square-root weights. It also distinguishes when a type simplex with at least three vertices is genuinely Euclidean-regular and yields a closed cube formula in exponentially many ambient edge coordinates.
